alignments.note: οὕτως is expanded into the supplied frame *After this manner*. *manner* is the generic completion and *After* the supplied preposition, so rule 17's generic-noun clause holds the head on the demonstrative word *this*, exactly as rule 99 keeps a *what manner of* frame on the pronominal word in all six of its corpus units and none on *manner*, and as rule 104 requires the demonstrative and interrogative members of one paradigm to be analysed alike. Rule 100 records that the corpus otherwise spends *so* on οὕτως and heads it there, never on a supplied noun. A head on *manner* remains defensible and was the reading previously taken.

Modifier is a verbless prepositional phrase, so the article keeps the supplied relativizer (rule 31). The vocative Πάτερ is anarthrous and the ASV writes no address word, so rule 89's apposition clause does not empty this article.
Supplied copula goes with the prepositional predicate (rules 31, 53).
Rule 17 heads on the lexical verb rather than the copula.

review_notes: Head of s001 changed from *manner* to *this*: the *manner of* frame is supplied, and rule 99's six corpus units head such a frame on the pronominal or demonstrative word and none on *manner*, rule 104 requiring the demonstrative member of the paradigm to be analysed like the interrogative. The competing head on *manner* is recorded in the unit's note.

σήμερον → *this day* at 6:11 is not the same case and keeps its head on *day*: there the Greek word carries a day-element for *day* to gloss, so rule 66's compound-core arm decides it, whereas οὕτως carries no manner-element at all.
The vocative Πάτερ is anarthrous and takes no supplied address word here, so rule 89 does not bear; the following article keeps the relativizer under rule 31's verbless-modifier clause.
